primary_audit.summary: Mostly faithful and vivid, but the rope-cutting rescue at the bridge has contradictory mechanics, with minor timing and ending-clause issues.

findings.exact_text: On the far side of the bridge, from a cliff edge, he could look out
findings.reason: The stacked opening location phrases create a compressed, awkward spatial construction; stating that he reached the cliff edge makes the position immediately clear.

findings.exact_text: search it alone
findings.reason: The pronoun “it” has an imprecise physical referent here. Naming the camp produces the natural English object of “search” and improves immediate clarity.

findings.exact_text: She leaned out and hauled, his hand found her wrist
findings.reason: A comma incorrectly joins two independent clauses, making the rapid action sequence grammatically unstable. A semicolon preserves the pace and clarifies the progression.

language_sentence_scan.rewrite: On the far side of the bridge, he reached a cliff edge where he could look out over the whole interior, and what he saw stopped him cold: the old knots didn't stop.
Nisa caught up and followed him in despite everything, because whatever she thought of him right now, she wasn't going to let him search the camp alone.
The bridge fell away beneath him into the cloud sea, and Arda swung free on the line Nisa still held. She leaned out and hauled; his hand found her wrist, and her grip found him.

secondary_audit.summary: The prose is highly fluent and publication-ready overall. Three local wording or punctuation defects need repair: one compressed spatial opening, one unclear pronoun, and one comma splice.
